rationale: M49.S1 #715 (geb CachingDriverFactory real-corpus shape): groovy's pinned grammar folds type args into the supertype token (`implements Cache<T>` -> text `Cache<T>`), and the pre-S1 oracle emitted the bracketed target raw — decls keys are bracket-stripped at registration, so the implements edge never matched its interface and SimpleCache.get -> Cache.get surfaced unexplained. Pins: clean heritage targets (implements Cache), nested-interface override resolution for both nested classes, and the enclosing-class method attribution.
notes: The forbid pins document the exact pre-S1 defect: bracketed heritage targets could never match decls keys (bracket-stripped at registration). Oracle mirror: collect() in deriveTreeEdges strips type args from every TYPE-node heritage target.
